title.en: Define a microcontroller and compare it with a microprocessor
Calculate the machine cycle time and timer delays of the 8051

say.en: A washing machine, a microwave oven and a TV remote each contain a tiny computer with its own memory, timers and ports, all on one chip: a microcontroller. In this lesson: Define a microcontroller and compare it with a microprocessor.
List the features of the 8051.
Calculate the machine cycle time and timer delays of the 8051.

body.en: A *microcontroller* is a single chip that contains a CPU together with ROM, RAM, parallel I/O ports, timers/counters, a serial port and interrupt logic: a complete computer on a chip, designed for embedded control. A microprocessor contains only the CPU and needs external memory and I/O chips, which makes it flexible for general-purpose computing but larger and costlier. Microcontrollers are used in washing machines, microwave ovens, remote controls, automobiles, toys and instruments.

points.en: *Microcontroller* = CPU + memory + I/O + timers on one chip

narration.en: A microcontroller puts the CPU, memory, ports and timers on one chip, ready for embedded control. A microprocessor is only the CPU and needs other chips around it.
narration.kn: ಮೈಕ್ರೋಕಂಟ್ರೋಲರ್ CPU, ಸ್ಮರಣೆ, ಪೋರ್ಟ್‌ಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಟೈಮರ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಒಂದೇ ಚಿಪ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಹೊಂದಿದೆ. ಮೈಕ್ರೋಪ್ರೊಸೆಸರ್ ಕೇವಲ CPU; ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಬೇರೆ ಚಿಪ್‌ಗಳು ಬೇಕು.

body.en: The Intel 8051 is an 8-bit microcontroller in a 40-pin package. It has 4 KB of on-chip ROM (program memory), 128 bytes of on-chip RAM, four 8-bit I/O ports P0–P3 (32 I/O lines), two 16-bit timers/counters T0 and T1, one full-duplex serial port (UART) and five interrupt sources (two external, two timer, one serial). It can address 64 KB of external program memory and 64 KB of external data memory (separate program and data spaces: Harvard architecture). Registers include A, B, R0–R7 (in four banks), the 16-bit DPTR and PC, SP and PSW. One machine cycle takes 12 oscillator periods, so a 12 MHz crystal gives a 1 µs machine cycle.

points.en: Two 16-bit timers, one UART, 5 interrupt sources

problem.en: A 12 MHz 8051 runs Timer 0 as a 16-bit timer from 0000H until it overflows. Find the time.

steps.en: Machine cycle = 12/12 MHz = 1 µs; the timer counts one per machine cycle.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A 12 MHz 8051 runs Timer 0 as a 16-bit timer from 0000H until it overflows. Find the time.

say.en: Let us work this out together. A 12 megahertz 8051 runs Timer 0 as a 16-bit timer from 0000H until it overflows. Find the time.
Machine cycle equals 12 over 12 megahertz equals 1 microsecond; the timer counts one per machine cycle.
Counts from 0000H to overflow equals 65 536.
Time equals 65 536 times 1 microsecond equals 65.536 milliseconds.
So the answer is 65.536 milliseconds.
